title: Atlantis Was Never Found… So Where Did the Story Come From? #atlantis #history
description:
Atlantis sank beneath the sea... but did it? Where does the story of the lost city of Atlantis really come from?

Beyond the Pillars of Hercules, a ring-shaped city of canals, bronze walls and a temple to Poseidon; fleets that conquered half the Mediterranean; then, in a single day and night, the sea swallowed it. Or so the story goes. There is no ruin, no map, no inscription: every word comes from Plato, around 360 BC, who says an Egyptian priest told it to Solon. No writer before Plato mentions it. In 1882, US congressman Ignatius Donnelly turned it into a lost super-civilization. So did Atlantis sink... or was it never there at all?

Sources
- Plato, Timaeus 20d-25d and Critias 113c-121c (c. 360 BC)
- Athanasius Kircher, Mundus Subterraneus (1665/1678), map of Atlantis
- Ignatius Donnelly, Atlantis: The Antediluvian World (1882)

Pictures: Gustave Doré, The Deluge; Athanasius Kircher, map of Atlantis (1678); Ignatius Donnelly's map of Atlantis (1882) and portrait; busts of Plato and Solon (public domain, Wikimedia Commons). Bronze of Zeus or Poseidon from Artemision, photo Jebulon (CC0). Map drawn from Natural Earth data (public domain).
